newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Rare pheasant species rediscovered in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Rare pheasant species rediscovered in Vietnam.

text.p: A species of pheasant long thought to have become extinct has been rediscovered in central Vietnam, the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) said on Wednesday.
WWF country representative David Hulse said villagers in the lush forests of Bach Ma National Park caught a male and a female of the so-called Edwards's pheasant last week.

The last known capture of a live Edwards's, a dark blue-black plumaged bird about the size of a chicken, was in 1928. It was already considered rare in 1923 when French ornithologist Jean Delacour took 15 of them back to Paris. It has only been found in Vietnam,
Three expeditions conducted between 1988 and 1994 failed to even sight one.

"This is yet another feather in the cap for conservation in Vietnam," WWF International's Asia/Pacific Programme Director Dawood Ghaznavi said in a statement. "Rediscovering this pheasant after 70 years means mankind has a second chance to save this exquisite bird and its habitat."
Hulse said the female of the newly-discovered pair had since died of injuries sustained while being captured and the male had a broken leg.
However, he said their discovery indicated that there was a high probability of an existing wild population and that conservationists now knew which habitat to protect.
